strings.activity.title: Submarine Explorer
strings.activity.description: Pilot your submarine and explore the deep ocean!
strings.encounter.octopus.hint: The octopus is tickling the glass! Honk the horn, release bubbles, or sound the alarm!
strings.encounter.shark.hint: The shark is waving its fin! Turn on the lights or sound the alarm!
strings.order.ahead: Full ahead! Turn on the engines!
strings.order.left: Turn to port! Steer to the left!
strings.order.right: Turn to starboard! Steer to the right!
strings.order.sonar: Listen to the deep! Press SONAR!
strings.order.compliment: Great maneuver, Captain! Course is set!
strings.voice.order.ahead: Full ahead! Turn on the engines!
strings.voice.order.left: Turn to port! Steer to the left!
strings.voice.order.right: Turn to starboard! Steer to the right!
strings.voice.order.compliment: Great maneuver, Captain! Course is set!
strings.voice.fact.whale.1: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth!
strings.voice.fact.whale.2: Whale songs can travel for hundreds of kilometers underwater!
strings.voice.fact.whale.3: Whales breathe air through the blowhole on top of their head!
strings.voice.fact.whale.4: A big whale's heart is as large as a small car!
strings.voice.fact.turtle.1: Sea turtles can hold their breath underwater for many hours!
strings.voice.fact.turtle.2: Sea turtles travel for thousands of kilometers across the open ocean!
strings.voice.fact.turtle.3: A sea turtle lays her eggs on the very same beach where she was born!
strings.voice.fact.turtle.4: A turtle shell is made of more than fifty bones fused together!
strings.voice.fact.dolphin.1: Dolphins use clicks and whistles to call each other by name!
strings.voice.fact.dolphin.2: Dolphins sleep with one eye open and half their brain awake to breathe!
strings.voice.fact.dolphin.3: Dolphins love to leap and play in the bow waves of ships!
strings.voice.fact.dolphin.4: Dolphins use natural sonar called echolocation to find fish!
strings.voice.fact.manta.1: The giant manta ray glides through water as if flying with huge wings!
strings.voice.fact.manta.2: Mantas are gentle and curious creatures that eat microscopic plankton!
strings.voice.fact.manta.3: Every manta has a unique pattern of spots on its belly, like a fingerprint!
strings.voice.fact.manta.4: Mantas sometimes leap out of the water in spectacular jumps!
strings.voice.fact.clownfish.1: Clownfish live safely among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones!
strings.voice.fact.clownfish.2: A clownfish has special mucus on its skin that protects it from stings!
strings.voice.fact.clownfish.3: Clownfish communicate with each other by making popping sounds!
strings.voice.fact.clownfish.4: All clownfish are born male and can change into females!
strings.voice.fact.coral.1: Corals look like rocks or plants, but they are colonies of tiny animals!
strings.voice.fact.coral.2: Coral reefs protect shorelines from big waves and storms!
strings.voice.fact.coral.3: Thousands of colorful sea animals find home and food among the corals!
strings.voice.fact.coral.4: Corals build magnificent underwater reefs visible from space!
strings.voice.fact.kelp.1: Giant kelp can grow up to half a meter in a single day!
strings.voice.fact.kelp.2: Giant kelp plants have air bulbs that float their fronds up toward the sun!
strings.voice.fact.kelp.3: Many sea creatures shelter safely inside underwater kelp forests!
strings.voice.fact.kelp.4: Underwater kelp forests produce lots of fresh oxygen for the oceans!
strings.voice.fact.krill.1: Krill are tiny swimming shrimp-like creatures that travel in massive clouds!
strings.voice.fact.krill.2: Krill are the favorite food of giant whales and many ocean fish!
strings.voice.fact.krill.3: Some krill can glow in the dark ocean with brilliant bioluminescent light!
strings.voice.fact.krill.4: Altogether, all the krill on Earth weigh more than all humans combined!
